context: data_leg_206m_8b val printed 2.033 at both step 8000 and 8500 -- the first zero delta after five consecutive drops of 0.008 to 0.015, against a print precision of 0.0005.
why_not_yet_a_signal: a true improvement below 0.0005 prints as 0.000, so one flat point at 3 decimals is not distinguishable from a small real gain. The ruled criterion is non-increasing and it is not violated.
threshold: if step 9000 prints val >= 2.033 as well, that is two consecutive zero-or-positive deltas and the run gets investigated: check gnorm, lr schedule position, and whether warmdown 0.1 has begun. If step 9000 prints <= 2.032, the flat point was resolution and nothing is done.
registered_before: the step-9000 val line did not exist anywhere when this was written -- the run was at step 8720 and the last printed val was 8500. Unlike the b0-20 threshold (shape 149), this one is a real pre-registration.
outcome: RESOLVED 2026-09-03T10:0xZ: step 9000 printed val 2.023, a -0.010 delta, back in the normal band (the five preceding drops were 0.008-0.015). Threshold said <= 2.032 means it was print resolution and nothing is done. Nothing is done.
amendment: b0 read all 17 deltas: the step-4000 delta was +0.0060, already the same order as zero at 12x print precision, and the curve recovered to +0.0210 at 4500. So a small delta is not new. The THRESHOLD STANDS as a watch item -- two consecutive sub-0.0005 improvements means the curve has not moved at three decimals for 1000 steps, which is worth a look and is what was registered ('investigate', not 'stop'). What changes is the CRITERION it sits under, see criterion_change.
criterion_change: The ruled health criterion said 'val monotone'. Print precision is 0.0005, so any true delta in (-0.0005, +0.0005) prints as 0.000 and monotonicity is UNMEASURABLE once deltas fall below a thousandth. The run is now in that region. RULING (fb, from b0's reading): the gate becomes 'val shows no rise exceeding print precision', i.e. no delta of -0.001 or worse. That holds on all 17 points and is decidable. The flat-point threshold above is a separate watch, not a gate -- a gate must be decidable, a watch may be a prompt to look.

context: Arm A = today's layer-level hybrid at d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 attn_every=4 (9 KDA blocks + 3 MLA blocks). Arm B = head_mixed=3: BOTH mixers in EVERY block on a 3:1 KDA:MLA head split (KDA h=6 inner=768, MLA h=2 inner=256, latent unchanged at 256). Both mixers read the full residual and write it back; their outputs are summed, which equals concatenating and applying one o (o(concat(a,b)) == o1(a)+o2(b), verified max|diff| 1.43e-06). Question: does putting attention in every layer at 1/4 width beat concentrating it in every fourth layer at full width, at equal depth and near-equal parameters.
params: RECOMPUTED on 2bc3fe6f, not carried over. arm A 206,128,200; arm B 208,552,008; +2,423,808 = +1.18% of the model, +4.10% of mixer parameters. An earlier draft said -1.91%: that was computed for a layout where each mixer read only its own slice, and it does not survive the change to full-residual projections. THE SIGN FLIPPED. Mechanism: every arm-B block costs 5,134,086, which is BELOW arm A's KDA block (5,265,416) and ABOVE its MLA block (3,932,160), so 9 KDA blocks save 131,330 each and 3 MLA blocks pay 1,201,926 each. Arm B is larger because it gives all 12 blocks an MLA where arm A had 3.
what_params_buys_at_1b: what +-2% params buys at 1B: unmeasured; nearest point is Stage E arm 1, +26.46% params for +0.031 nat worse, not a slope
confound: DEPTH IS NOT THE CONFOUND -- both arms are L12, same ffn, same d. THE REAL CONFOUND IS ATTENTION COUNT: arm B has 12 attention paths of width 256, arm A has 3 of width 1024. Total attention width is 3072 vs 3072, equal by construction, but the COUNT and the PER-LAYER width both move together and this design cannot separate them. A result favouring B does not distinguish 'attention in every layer helps' from 'more, narrower attention heads help'. Separating them needs a third arm (e.g. attn_every=1 at full width, which is +8 blocks of MLA and a different parameter budget) and is not in this A/B.
threshold: Decided on val BPB at the shared token budget, both arms same seed, same data order, same cards-per-arm (2 each). Arm B WINS if val BPB is lower by more than 0.003 (6x the 0.0005 print precision, and larger than the 0.0021 arm-to-arm spread measured on the two doccu legs). Arm B LOSES if higher by more than 0.003. Between -0.003 and +0.003 is NO DIFFERENCE and the layer-level form stays, on the ordinary ground that the incumbent needs no reason and the challenger costs +1.18% params.
registered_before: No arm-B training step has been run at the time of writing. What HAS run: one forward+backward at B=2 T=4096 on card 5 (runs/audit_0904/b0_headmix_first_run.py, rc=0), which produced loss 10.603622, 232 parameters all with finite gradients, block0.kda max|grad| 2.374649e-04 and block0.mla max|grad| 1.304626e-03 (both halves learn, neither is decorative), 1,034 tok/s single-card no-DDP, peak 15.91 GiB. That is a smoke test of the path, not a measurement of the arm: no val number for either arm exists yet.

outcome: ARM B LOSES, by the pre-registered rule rather than by a reading of it. doc_cu block-paired B-A = +0.087380 nats/token (higher is worse), row-weighted over n=576 blocks / 9 domains / 2,359,296 tokens, sd 0.025853, SE 0.001077, t +81.12; sign 576 up, 0 down, 0 tie, one-sided p 4.04e-174. The LOSE threshold is +0.003; the measured delta is 29x it and the whole 95% interval (+0.0853, +0.0895) sits above it, so the verdict does not depend on where the line was drawn. Token-weighted equals row-weighted because every block is 4096 tokens -- an identity here, not a corroboration. ALL NINE DOMAINS AGREE IN SIGN, range +0.0642 to +0.1128: chat_qa +0.1128, chatml +0.1114, zh_web +0.1022, textbook_30b +0.0981, en_c4_stage2 +0.0848, math_owm_stage2 +0.0752, code_py_rp1t +0.0697, cot +0.0681, code_py_starcoder +0.0642. context: Arm A = today's layer-level hybrid at d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 attn_every=4 (9 KDA blocks + 3 MLA blocks). Arm B = head_mixed=3: BOTH mixers in EVERY block on a 3:1 KDA:MLA head split (KDA h=6 inner=768, MLA h=2 inner=256, latent unchanged at 256). Both mixers read the full residual and write it back; their outputs are summed, which equals concatenating and applying one o (o(concat(a,b)) == o1(a)+o2(b), verified max|diff| 1.43e-06). confound: DEPTH IS NOT THE CONFOUND -- both arms are L12, same ffn, same d. THE REAL CONFOUND IS ATTENTION COUNT: arm B has 12 attention paths of width 256, arm A has 3 of width 1024. context: Sparse product-key memory layers added in parallel to the FFN at layers 3,6,9 (one shared pool) of the d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 attn_every=4 backbone. Control = ckpt_b0_headmix_armA.pt (1B tokens on mix_200m_8b, seed 42, world 2, 3815 steps). Arms reuse the control's launch line byte-for-byte plus the memory flags, so scoring is block-paired on identical data order.

arms.M1: 1,048,576 values (1024x1024 product keys) x d1024, 1.07B memory params

dense_params_equal_control: REQUIRED: dense parameter count identical to the control; the arm differs only by the memory. Recompute on the launch sha and record here before launch.
readout_1_primary: block-paired doc_cu val, arm minus control. Adopt if <= -0.010 nat (size of the N2 params effect). Null if |delta| < 0.003. Between: measured, not adopted.
readout_2_split: closed-book fact probe (cloze over a textbook_30b holdout slice registered in the holdout registry BEFORE launch; report chance floor AND control score first; if the control is within 1 SE of chance the readout is UNDEFINED at this scale, not null) vs reasoning probe (l1_fewshot answer-present, 3 demos). Claim 'memory buys knowledge, not reasoning' = fact delta exceeds reasoning delta by more than both SEs.
readout_3_scaling: M2 vs M1 vs control: slope of doc_cu against memory size. Two points plus control are a line, not a law.
readout_4_diagnostics: runs/memory_diag.jsonl every 100 steps: pool_touched_frac, topk_entropy, key_gini, tok_s_gpu. pool_touched_frac < 0.20 at step 1000 = collapse: stop and report, never tune in place.
readout_5_throughput: tok/s/gpu at step 30 vs the control's 82K. Below 70K: stop and report.
registered_before: No memory-layer code exists in any branch at registration; no arm has run a step; the holdout slice is not yet carved. Written by the controller so the criterion is fixed before the probe, the model or the slice exist.
confound: FLOP is not held exactly equal (memory adds <= +3%); memory params are not comparable to dense params one-for-one, which is the point being measured. The fact probe's domain (textbook_30b) is a training domain; only the registered holdout slice makes it closed-book.
amendment: READOUT 2 RE-SCOPED (fb ruling on e1's measurement): mix_200m_8b has no encyclopedic domain in any language -- textbook_30b is 100% Chinese synthetic tutorials (n=160, cjk=1.000), wiki is not in the mix, en_c4_stage2 is web boilerplate. The fact probe becomes an API-NAME CLOZE over a held-out slice of code_py_starcoder (33% of the mix, English): items where a prefix ends at `<module>.` or inside a call and the gold is the true attribute/function/keyword-argument name, scored by continuation log-likelihood against 3 distractors that are real names from the same module or object. API names are arbitrary propositions that must be memorised, which is what a memory layer is claimed to store; the reasoning probe is unchanged. Chance and control floors, and the UNDEFINED rule, apply as written. The charter's 'English encyclopedic domain' sentence was wrong at registration and is corrected in the same commit.
amendment_2: READOUT 2 IS A DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES (fb ruling on e1's design point, supersedes the item-type half of amendment 1 and keeps its domain): a closed-book cloze over unread rows measures generalisation, which readout 1 already measures; 'memory buys knowledge' is a claim about RECALL of training content. Domain: code_py_starcoder (English, 25.4% of its 2,139,719-row pool is read, so 1,597,568 rows are never read by control or arms; no slice is carved and no registry entry is written). Items: API-name cloze, 4-way against real names from the same module, drawn from two regions of the SAME cache -- SEEN = rows in seqs[n_val:cap] the arms train on, UNSEEN = rows in the never-read tail; the row-index boundary, sample_seed, val_frac and cap are PINNED into the item file, never recomputed at score time. delta_seen = arm-control on SEEN, delta_unseen = arm-control on UNSEEN, both block-paired on identical data order; the claim holds if delta_seen - delta_unseen > 0 beyond both SEs. Absolute SEEN scores are training-set numbers and are never reported as capability. Chance and control floors and the UNDEFINED rule apply to both regions. Fallback if code_py_starcoder yields under 2000 clean items per region: textbook_30b (Chinese, 56.9% unread) with the same design; the claim is language-agnostic.
